abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer is one of the most aggressive and lethal gastrointestinal malignancies, and ferroptosis resistance contributes to chemoresistance. Tumor-educated macrophages(TAMs) are key components of the tumor microenvironment, but whether and how they regulate ferroptosis in pancreatic cancer cells remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of tumor-educated macrophages (TEMs) in pancreatic cancer cell ferroptosis and the underlying molecular mechanism.
METHODS: TEMs were generated by coculturing THP-1 cells with the pancreatic cancer cell lines PANC1 and CFPAC, and TEM-conditioned medium (TEM-CM) was collected to treat pancreatic cancer cells. Ferroptosis was induced by erastin, and ferroptotic events were assessed by lipid ROS, MDA, iron accumulation, GSH levels, and transmission electron microscopy. RNA sequencing was performed to identify differentially expressed genes. The expression and activity of VEGFR2, C-Raf, ERK1/2, mTOR, LC3, p62, KEAP1, and NRF2 were investigated by treating cells with pharmacological inhibitors (Ki8751, LY3009120, chloroquine, and ferrostatin-1), performing gene knockdown and overexpression, and conducting Western blot co-immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination, and cycloheximide chase assays. In vivo experiments were conducted using an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic cancer (n = 5 per group).
RESULTS: TEM-CM reduced the sensitivity of PANC1 and CFPAC cells to erastin-induced ferroptosis, as evidenced by decreased lipid ROS, MDA, and iron accumulation and increased GSH levels. Neutralization of VEGF, but not IL-10 or TGFβ, significantly reversed the ferroptosis-inhibiting effect of TEM-CM. RNA sequencing identified TM7SF2 as a key mediator. TEM-CM upregulated TM7SF2 mRNA and protein levels, activated mTOR, and suppressed autophagy, leading to p62 accumulation. Accumulated p62 competitively bound KEAP1, disrupted the KEAP1-NRF2 interaction, inhibited NRF2 ubiquitination and degradation, and promoted NRF2 nuclear translocation, thereby upregulating GPX4, HMOX1, and GCLM. Mechanistically, TEM-derived VEGF bound VEGFR2 and activated the C-Raf/ERK1/2 pathway by upregulating TM7SF2, which in turn promoted mTOR phosphorylation. These effects were reversed by TM7SF2 knockdown, VEGF neutralization, VEGFR2 inhibition, or C-Raf inhibition.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that TEM-derived VEGF promotes ferroptosis resistance in pancreatic cancer cells through the VEGFR2-TM7SF2-C-Raf/ERK1/2-mTOR-autophagy-p62-NRF2 axis. This axis may represent a potential therapeutic target for overcoming ferroptosis resistance in pancreatic cancer. However, our conclusions are mainly based on in vitro cell models, and further validation in additional cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and in vivo models is warranted.
key_points_ko: 종양 교육 대식세포(TEM)는 췌장암 세포가 erastin으로 유도된 페로토시스에 저항성을 갖도록 만들었습니다.
TEM 유래 VEGF는 VEGFR2를 결합하고 C-Raf/ERK1/2 및 mTOR 경로를 활성화했습니다.
이로 인해 p62가 축적되고 KEAP1-NRF2 상호작용이 방해받아 NRF2가 활성화되며 항산화 유전자가 증가했습니다.
이 연구는 주로 체외 세포 모델을 기반으로 수행되었습니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 종양 교육 대식세포(tumor-educated macrophages, TEMs)가 췌장암 세포의 페로토시스(ferroptosis) 저항성에 미치는 영향과 그 분자적 기전을 조사했습니다. 연구 결과, TEM 유래 VEGF는 VEGFR2-TM7SF2-C-Raf/ERK1/2-mTOR-자가포식-p62-NRF2 축을 활성화하여 췌장암 세포의 페로토시스 저항성을 촉진하는 것으로 나타났습니다. 이 기전은 췌장암의 페로토시스 저항성을 극복하기 위한 잠재적인 치료 표적이 될 수 있습니다. 그러나 이 결론은 주로 체외(in vitro) 세포 모델을 기반으로 하므로 추가적인 검증이 필요합니다.
title: Tumor-educated macrophages promote ferroptosis inhibition in pancreatic cancer via activating the p62-KEAP1-NRF2 pathway
title_ko: 종양 교육 대식세포는 p62-KEAP1-NRF2 경로 활성화를 통해 췌장암에서 페로토시스 억제를 촉진합니다
